paper.title: Study on bandgap predications of ABX3-type perovskites by machine learning
paper.file_name: 33_Study on bandgap predications of ABX3-type perovskites by machine learning.pdf
paper.research_summary: The present work adopts machine learning (ML) to predict bandgaps of perovskites, where we collect 227 sets of experimental bandgap data of perovskites from the latest 1254 publications, to establish and identify 4 models from 24 kinds of ML models. The results of the models achieve high accuracy with root mean square error (RMSE) of down to 0.55 and meanwhile, the pearson correlation coefficient of up to 99%. In addition, our ML models give the effect of each chemical composition constituting the ABX3-type perovskites on the bandgaps by using the SHAP value, and they can be well explained in physics.

tasks.objective: To fast and accurately predict the bandgaps of ABX3-type perovskites for solar cell devices

evidence.text: The accurate bandgap prediction of perovskites has great significance for solar cell devices.

stages.stage_goal: Establish and clean database of ABX3-type perovskite compositions and bandgaps

evidence.text: The second step is the establishment and cleaning of the database. First, data with the same chemical composition and bandgap are removed, but due to the different conditions and environments of the experiments, there will be data with the same chemical composition (input data) but different bandgap values (output data). In order to ensure the authenticity of the data and avoid the non-uniform distribution of the data, we choose to keep them in the training dataset.
We set up a training dataset and a test dataset of ABX3-type perovskites containing 204 and 23 data to train and evaluate the pros and cons of the algorithm.

stages.stage_goal: Train multiple ML models (Xgboost, RF, MLP, LR, SVR, KNN) on the cleaned dataset

evidence.text: We use six ML algorithms by Scikit-learn and Xgboost modules to build BPMs on the pycharm platform. Linear regression (LR): LR is a model that uses the best linear relationship between input and output to fit. K-nearest neighbors (KNN): KNN is simply summarized as “those who are close to you are red, those who are close to you are black”, i.e. your category is inferred from your neighbors. Support vector regression (SVR): SVR uses a linear function in vector space to fit the samples. The model takes the combined distance of all the samples’ actual positions to this linear function as the loss and minimizes the loss to get the parameters of the linear function. Random forest (RF): Random forest is representative of ensemble learning ideas. By integrating many decision trees into a forest, they learn from each other’s strengths, and finally optimize the prediction model. Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), which is the most commonly used type of neural network, consists of an input layer, an output layer, and one or more hidden layers. Xtreme Gradient Boosting (Xgboost): Xgboost is a branch of ensemble learning different from RF, which is an improvement of the Gradient Boosting decision tree algorithm.

stages.stage_goal: Evaluate model performance using RMSE and Pearson correlation coefficient
stage_output: RMSE and r values for each model

evidence.text: Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) is the most commonly used evaluation indicator for ML model which measures the deviation between the observed value and the predicted value. In this statistics, Pearson’s correlation coefficient (r) is often used to represent the correlation between two variables, which we use to test the performance of ML models.
Xgboost has a degree of dispersion similar to the experimental value, the lowest RMSE, and the highest correlation coefficient, so Xgboost performs best in this set of data.

stages.stage_goal: Compare ML predictions with DFT-calculated bandgaps for new perovskite compositions
stage_output: RMSE comparison between ML and DFT
superiority of ML over DFT demonstrated

evidence.text: To verify the accuracy of our ML model and predication ability for new perovskites, we synthesize the Cs0.05(FA0.85MA0.15)0.95Pb (I0.85Br0.15)3 perovskite thin films for bandgap determination.

We have also conducted the comparison with the DFT calculations on the bandgap values of the perovskites with 3 different compositions, which are new to our ML model. The prediction result of ML and the comparison are shown in Table S12. It is found that the bandgap values obtained by ML model are very close to the values of the DFT calculations.

stages.stage_goal: Synthesize and experimentally measure bandgap of a novel perovskite composition to validate ML prediction

evidence.text: To verify the accuracy of our ML model and predication ability for new perovskites, we synthesize the Cs0.05(FA0.85MA0.15)0.95Pb (I0.85Br0.15)3 perovskite thin films for bandgap determination. The experimental details of the present perovskite synthesis refer to the supporting information. In order to determine the bandgap value, the two measurements are used including absorption spectrum and photoluminescence (PL) spectrum. A Tauc plot of (Ahv)2 versus photon energy (hv) is obtained from the absorption to obtain experimental bandgap value. The measurement results refer to the supporting information. It is found that the peak (764 nm) of the PL spectrum shows a good agreement with the obtained bandgap from the Tauc plot. The bandgap of the present perovskite thin films is in a small variation range of 1.61–1.62 eV. According to the predication of our ML model (BPM-ABX3-type perovskites), the obtained bandgap value is 1.60 eV (Keep two decimal places), which has a difference with the experimental value less than 1.2% relative.

stages.stage_goal: Use SHAP to quantify and explain the influence of each chemical composition on bandgap predictions
stage_output: SHAP values showing contribution of B-site metal and X-site halogen ions

evidence.text: Through the means of ML explanation (SHapley Additive exPlanations, abbreviated as SHAP), it is found that the contents of B-site metal and X-site halogen ion have the key influence on the bandgaps of ABX3-type perovskites.

SHAP can show how 8 compositions (inputs) contribute to the bandgaps of ABX3-type perovskites (outputs). Therefore, we select the Xgboost and RF algorithm models that perform best in the database of ABX3-type perovskites, and then use SHAP to explain the BPM (using RF and Xgboost).
